title.narrative: A Working Future in Uganda - Plan & Accenture

description.narrative: Cooperation between PLAN and Accenture to support youth employment and youth econimic empowerment in Uganda through collaboration between the public, civil society and private sector.
Samarbete mellan PLAN och Accenture avseende program för ungdomssysselsättning och stärkande av ungas ekonomiska egenmakt i Uganda genom samverkan mellan stat, civila samhället och privat näringsliv.

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The collaboration with PLAN Uganda for implementing the programme "A Working Future” (reaching out to 12,000,000 youth in Kamuli and Tororo districts in Western Uganda) has delivered good results related to plan. Through the project, ways of collaborating with the private sector has been explored in order to create win-win partnerships.
Over 12.000 youth have been recruited into Village, savings and loan associations (VSLA). 99 percent were employed within producer groups, in Micro-franchising and around one hundred in formal employment.
Effects are visible on the outcome level, including increased economic resilience because of improved savings (via increased income generating activities) and accumulated productive assets. Access to capital, skills training and business linkages has led to self employment that many members of VSLAs noted has made them independent and self-reliant.
When the program first started, 100% of the youth were below the poverty line (1,90 USD). That number went down to 61% which is a 39% increase in youth above the poverty line from when the program started. The average monthly income increased by 621% (completion report and end term evaluation, 2016).
A Working Future was carried out as a pilot that should be able to inform future work on youth employment. The model was proved successful in order to build partnerships with the private sector in which win-win solutions can be sought. VSLAs evidently served as an adequate platform to facilitate the transformation for youth employment. The use of digital solutions has proven to be an enabler to support achievement of project objectives.
